               <ns0:head>CHAP. XII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 AT that time Jesus went on the Sabbath-day through the corn, and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relating this Story, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.23. varieth little. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> relating it, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.1. saith it was on the Second Sabbath after the first, and his Disciples did eat rubbing them. God in his Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 23.25. had said, <ns0:hi>when thou comest into thy Neighbours Standing Corn, thou mayest pluck the Ears with thy Hand, but thou shalt not move a Sickle to thy Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours Standing Corn.</ns0:hi> To take for our need so much of our Neighbours Goods, as we may reasonably think that if he were present, and knew our Circumstances, he would give us, is no <ns0:hi>Theft.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> therefore do not accuse them of <ns0:hi>Theft,</ns0:hi> but of <ns0:hi>Violation of the Sabbath. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, This happened upon the second Sabbath after the first. Whether that was the <ns0:hi>Sabbath</ns0:hi> next following the <ns0:hi>Feast of Vnlea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vened Bread,</ns0:hi> (which was about the time of our <ns0:hi>Easter</ns0:hi>) the first and last days, of which were <ns0:hi>Sabbaths</ns0:hi> in the Jewish Sense, or the <ns0:hi>Feast of Tabernacles,</ns0:hi> or any other is not much Material for us to know. But on a <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day</ns0:hi> it was, that our Saviour went through the Corn, and his <ns0:hi>Disciples were an hungry,</ns0:hi> this may teach us their low Estate, and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition in the World. He could quickly have supplyed their hunger, but he chose to leave them to relieve themselves with <ns0:hi>Plucking, Rubbing</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eating</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Corn,</ns0:hi> that he might have an <ns0:hi>opportunity,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>instruct</ns0:hi> them, and the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> in the true Doctrine of the Sabbath.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 But when the pharisees saw <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples, do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day.<ns0:note place="bottom">So saith <ns0:hi>Mark, Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.24. only he puts it into the form of a <ns0:hi>Question. Luke</ns0:hi> adds nothing, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.2. but saith, <ns0:hi>Certain of the Pharisees.</ns0:hi> They granted the thing lawful to be done ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Day, but not on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day.</ns0:hi> How blind is Super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stition, that they could think, that it was contrary to the Will of God, that his People should fit themselves for the Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vice of the <ns0:hi>Sabbath</ns0:hi> by a <ns0:hi>moderate refreshment?</ns0:hi> Some of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> ordinarily attended Christ's Motions, not to be in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />structed by him, but (as is afterward said) <ns0:hi>That they might have something whereof to accuse him.</ns0:hi> What a little thing do they Carp at? Wherein was the Sin<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the <ns0:hi>plucking</ns0:hi> of a few Ears of Corn, and <ns0:hi>rubbing them,</ns0:hi> could hardly be called <ns0:hi>Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Labour,</ns0:hi> especially not in the Sense of the <ns0:hi>Commandment,</ns0:hi> which restrained not <ns0:hi>necessary Labour,</ns0:hi> but such Labour as took them off from the Duties of the <ns0:hi>Sabbath,</ns0:hi> but their <ns0:hi>Tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition</ns0:hi> had made this unlawful, as it was a little <ns0:hi>reaping,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>kind of Threshing.</ns0:hi> Hypocrites and Formalists, are always most Zealous for little things in the Law, or for their own Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ditaments to it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 How he entred into the house of God, and did eat the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Em. 25<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Lev. 8.31.</ns0:note> shew-bread, which it was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> add little, only <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> specifyeth the time, <ns0:hi>In the days of Abraham, the High Priest,</ns0:hi> and saith, <ns0:hi>When he had need, and was an hungred.</ns0:hi> We have the History. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 21.6. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was upon his Flight from <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> upon the notice of his danger given him by <ns0:hi>Ionathan, Chap.</ns0:hi> 20. and being hungry, he asks of the <ns0:hi>High Priest five Loaves</ns0:hi> of bread, The <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> tells him he had none but <ns0:hi>Hallowed Bread,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> gave him, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. what this <ns0:hi>Shew-bread</ns0:hi> was, may be read, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 24.5, 6, 7, 8, 9. it is expres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly said, <ns0:hi>A Stranger shall not eat thereof.</ns0:hi> (Now saith our Saviour) notwithstanding this <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Followers being an hungred</ns0:hi> did <ns0:hi>eat</ns0:hi> thereof, tho strictly according to the Let<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter of the Law, none but the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> might Eat it: But some may object. <ns0:hi>What was this to the purpose?</ns0:hi> It was not up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day? An.</ns0:hi> It was either upon the Sabbath Day, or immediately after, for it was to be set on every <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day,</ns0:hi> and to be <ns0:hi>Eaten in the Holy Place, Levit.</ns0:hi> 24.8, 9. and the <ns0:hi>High Priest told David,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 21.6. That it was taken away to set <ns0:hi>hot Bread in the Room of it.</ns0:hi> 2. But Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />condly that which our Saviour produceth this for, was to prove a more <ns0:hi>General proposition,</ns0:hi> which being proved, the Law<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fulness of his <ns0:hi>Disciples Act,</ns0:hi> would easily be inferred from it. That was this. <ns0:hi>That the Letter of a Ritual Law is not to be insisted upon, where some eminent necessity urgeth the contra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, in the performance of some Natural or Moral Duty.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Law of Nature</ns0:hi> commandeth every Man to feed himself, when he is hungry. The <ns0:hi>Moral Law</ns0:hi> confirms this, as it is a means to the Observation of the 6<ns0:hi>th.</ns0:hi> Commandment, and especially on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day,</ns0:hi> so far as may fit us for the best Sanctifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of it. The Law concerning the <ns0:hi>Shew-bread,</ns0:hi> was but a <ns0:hi>Ritual Law,</ns0:hi> and that part of it which restrained the use of it, when taken off from the Holy Table, was of lightest concern, as it commanded it should be eaten by the Priests only, and by them in the holy place, where the Life, or necessary Relief of Men was concerned, the Obligation of the Ritual Law ceased, and that was Lawful both for <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> which in ordinary Cases had not been Lawful. Works necessa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry either for the upholding of our Lives, or fitting us for Sab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bath Services, are lawful upon the Sabbath day. Tho theLaw con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the <ns0:hi>Sabbath,</ns0:hi> be a Moral Law, yet it is <ns0:hi>jus positivum,</ns0:hi> not a <ns0:hi>Law Natural,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Positive,</ns0:hi> and must be so interpre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted, as not to destroy the <ns0:hi>Law Natural,</ns0:hi> which Commands Men to feed themselves: nor yet to destroy it self. The Scope and end of it, is to be considered, which is the keeping of a day, as a day of <ns0:hi>Holy and Religious rest.</ns0:hi> What Labour is necessary to such keeping of it, is also lawful. The <ns0:hi>time</ns0:hi> of the Sabbath, is not more holy than the <ns0:hi>Shew-bread,</ns0:hi> and as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> in a case of necessity, might make a common use of that Holy Bread, so the Disciples in a case of like necessity, might make use of a little of that <ns0:hi>holy time,</ns0:hi> in such necessa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry Servile Work, as might fit them for their Sabbath Service. Thus it was Lawful by the Law of God and if the Pharisees had not been ignorant, or had understood what they had read, they would never have disputed this, the instance of Holy <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> might have satisfyed. So that this little kind of Labour could only be a Breach of one of their <ns0:hi>by-Laws,</ns0:hi> by which they pretended to expound the Law of God, in which he shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth they had given a false interpretation.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 Or have ye not read in the Law, how that on the sabbath days <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 7.22.</ns0:note> the priests in the temple pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phane the sabbath, and are blameless.<ns0:note place="bottom">Neither <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> have this Argument of our Saviours. The meaning is: All Acts of Servile Labour, are not unlaw<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful on the Sabbath day. The <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> according to the Law, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 28.9. <ns0:hi>Offer Sacrifices,</ns0:hi> and do many other Acts, such as Circumcising, and many other things, which in your Sense would be a <ns0:hi>Prophanation of the Sabbath,</ns0:hi> yet you do not blame them, neither are they to be blamed, because God permitted. and directed them. If any say, but how doth this agree to what our Saviour is speaking to? <ns0:hi>An.</ns0:hi> the Disciples of Christ were imployed with, and by him in going about and Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Gospel, and what they now did, was but in order to fit them for his Work, when they had not had such leisure as o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, before hand to provide; and this Establisheth a second Rule, <ns0:hi>That Works of Piety, and tending to fit us for Acts of Piety, that cannot conveniently be done before, are lawful <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n the Sabbath Day.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But I say unto you, that in this place is <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Chro. 6.18.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> greater than the temple.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Jews had very Superstitious Conceits, concerning the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> and might object, But the Priests Works are done in the <ns0:hi>Temple.</ns0:hi> The Jews had a saying<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>That in the Temple there was no Sabbath.</ns0:hi> They looked upon the Temple, as Sanctifying all Actions done there. To obviate this (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>In this place is one</ns0:hi> (that is) I am <ns0:hi>greater than</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Temple.</ns0:hi> The Temple was but a Type of me. If the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> can sanctify so much Labour, will not my Autho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity, and Permission think you, excuse this little Labour of my Disciples.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:238" />7 But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.<ns0:note place="bottom">Neither <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> have this Argument. Our Lord yet goeth on Taxing these great Doctors of Ignorance. The Text, he quoteth is, <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> 6.6. we met with it before quoted by our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 9.13. The meaning is, <ns0:hi>That God preferreth Mercy before Sacrifice</ns0:hi>; where two Laws in respect of some Circumstances seem to clash one with ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, so as we cannot obey both, our Obedience is due to that which is the more Excellent Law. Now saith our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our, the <ns0:hi>Law of Mercy</ns0:hi> is the more Excellent Law. God preferreth it <ns0:hi>before Sacrifice,</ns0:hi> which had you well consider<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, you would never have accused my Disciples, who in this point are Guiltless.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For the Son of man is Lord, even of the sabbath day.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Argument <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath it thus, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.27, 28. <ns0:hi>And he said unto them, the Sabbath was made for Man, and not Man for the Sabbath. Therefore the Son of Man is Lord also of the Sabbath.</ns0:hi> Some Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters make these two Arguments, 1. <ns0:hi>The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath</ns0:hi>: Therefore it is in my Power, to dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pense with this Action of my Disciples, tho it had been con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trary to the letter of the Law: Or rather, Therefore it is in my Power to interpret the Law, which I my self made. 2. <ns0:hi>The Sabbath is made for Man, not Man for the Sabbath.</ns0:hi> A Law made for the good of another bindeth not, in such Cases where the Observation of it would be evidently for his Harm and Ruin. The Law of the Sabbath was made for the good of Man, that he might have a solemn time, in which he should be under an Obligation to pay his Homage unto God, this must not be so interpreted, as would tend to the Destruction of a man. I find Interpreters divided about that term <ns0:hi>the Son of Man.</ns0:hi> Some think that it is not to be in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreted, as usually in the Gospel concerning <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi> But of ordinary Men, and that Mans Lordship over the Sabbath, is proved by the Subserviency of it to his good, to which end also it was ordained. But certainly, that is both a <ns0:hi>Dan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gerous</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>unscriptural Interpretation,</ns0:hi> dangerous to give Man a <ns0:hi>Lordship</ns0:hi> over a <ns0:hi>Moral Law,</ns0:hi> for it is very improper to call any <ns0:hi>Lord</ns0:hi> of a thing, because he hath the use of it, and it is for his advantage; I cannot see but we may as well make Man Lord of the whole ten Commandements, as of one of them. <ns0:hi>Vnscriptural,</ns0:hi> for tho our Saviour useth this term more than threescore times in the Gospel, yet he always u<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seth it with Relation to himself, never with reference to any meer Man: Neither is there any necessity to understand it otherwise here. Christ affirming himself <ns0:hi>Lord of the Sab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bath,</ns0:hi> spake properly enough to the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Quarrel. For it must needs then follow, that he had Power to dispense with the Observation of it at particular times; and much more to give a true and right Interpretation of the <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> concerning it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And when he was departed thence, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 6.6.</ns0:note> he went into their Synagogue.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>He went again into their Syna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gogues on the Sabbath Day.</ns0:hi> This our Saviour was often wont to do, to own there what was done according to his Fathers institution, and himself to do what good he could: Nor doth he now decline it, because he had had so late a Contest with them: It is therefore said, that he went into <ns0:hi>their Synagogues,</ns0:hi> as being neither ashamed of what he had delivered, nor afraid to own it in the Face of his Adversaries.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And behold, there was a man which had <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> hand withered. And they asked him, saying, <ns0:note place="margin">Luk. 13, 14. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 14.3. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 9.16.</ns0:note> Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> repeating the same History saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.1, 2. <ns0:hi>There was a Man which had a withered Hand, and they watched him whether he would heal him on the Sabbath Day, that they might accuse him.</ns0:hi> So saith <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6, 7. only he addeth, that it was <ns0:hi>his right Hand,</ns0:hi> which made his afflicti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on greater: They asked him not, that they might rightly inform themselves, but <ns0:hi>that they might accuse him,</ns0:hi> to their Magistrates that had Power in those Cases, for the Vio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation of the Sabbath was, amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> a Capital Crime.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And he said unto them, What man shall there be amongst you, that shall have one sheep, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ee Exod. 23.5. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 22.4.</ns0:note> if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> out?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.3, 4, 5. <ns0:hi>And he said unto the Man, that had the withered Hand, Stand forth. And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the Sabbath Days, or to do Evil, to save Life or to Kill? But they held their Peace. Luke</ns0:hi> reports it thus, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.8. <ns0:hi>But he knew their Thoughts, and said to the Man which had the withered Hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst, and he arose, and stood-forth. Then said Iesus unto them, I will ask you one thing, Is it lawful on the Sabbath Days to do Good, or to do Evil, to save Life or to destroy it?</ns0:hi> Christ knew their Thoughts<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> He needed not that any Man should tell him what was in the Heart of Men, he knew their Design in coming, and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounding this Question. He calls this Man with the withered Hand to stand forth, that all Men might see, and take no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tice of him. Then he argueth the Case with the <ns0:hi>Pharis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>es,</ns0:hi> telling them, that they themselves would grant, that if a man had a sheep <ns0:hi>fallen into a Pit</ns0:hi> on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day,</ns0:hi> they might labour so far as to take it out (so it seemeth that in Christs time they did expound the Law.) They also knew that the Life, or good of a Man, was to be preferred be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the <ns0:hi>Life of a Beast,</ns0:hi> in their reproving him: Therefore they condemned themselves in a thing which they allowed. Then he propounds a Question to them, which <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> hath not, but it is mentioned both by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi> He asketh them, <ns0:hi>Whether it was lawful on the Sabbath Day to do Good, or to do Evil? To save Life or to destroy it.</ns0:hi> The Argument is this, Whatsoever is good to save the Life of Man, may be done on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day,</ns0:hi> but this is a good Action, if I should not lend him my help, when it is in my Power, I should in the Sense of Gods Law, kill him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Then saith he to the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> forth, and <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> was restored whole, like as the other.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>They held their Peace,</ns0:hi> they made him no Answer to his Question, upon which, <ns0:hi>He looking round a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout him with Anger, being grieved for the Hardness of their Hearts, he spake unto the Man—Stretch forth thine Hand. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Looking about them all,</ns0:hi> he said, &c. Our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> looked about him, to see if any of them would adventure to answer him, but he saw their Mouths were shut. He was angry that these great Doctors of the Law, should understand the Law of God no better, and should yet be so hardy, as to take upon them to instruct him. He was also grieved (saith <ns0:hi>Mark) at the Hardness of their Hearts</ns0:hi>; that which we call Hardness, is a Quality in a thing which resisteth the Truth, a non-impressiveness, when a thing will receive no impression from things apt to make impressions; the Hardness of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Hearts la<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in this, that whereas Christ's <ns0:hi>Words</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Works</ns0:hi> might reasonably, and ought to have made an impression upo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> them of Faith, that they should have owned and received him as the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>: Yet, they had no such Effect, nor made any such impressions upon them. He said to the Man, <ns0:hi>Stretch forth thine Hand, and he stretched it forth,</ns0:hi> &c. Christ sometimes used the <ns0:hi>Ceremony</ns0:hi> of laying on his Hand; here he doth not, to let us know that that was but a Sign of what was done by his <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi>: What little things malici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous Men will Carp at. What was her<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of <ns0:hi>servile Labour</ns0:hi> on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day</ns0:hi>? They did far more themselves, as of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten as they lifted, a Beast out of a Pit. Our Saviour com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounds, or prepareth no Medicaments, he only speaks the Word, and he is healed. But <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> tells that,</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Then <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 3.6. Luk. 6.11. Joh. 5.18. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.39. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.53.</ns0:note> the Pharisees went out, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>took Coun<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>el.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> held a councel against him, how they might destroy him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>They were filled with Madness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />muned one with another, what they might do to Iesus. Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>they straightway took Councel with the</ns0:hi> Hero<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dians <ns0:hi>against him, how they might destroy him.</ns0:hi> What cause of their Madness was here offered? A poor lame Man was miraculously healed. They certainly were mad to see them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves confuted, who would not acknowledge him to be the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> or to hear themselves <ns0:hi>Non-plust,</ns0:hi> or to find them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves <ns0:hi>Contradicted</ns0:hi> (a thing Proud men cannot bear) They take Councel with the <ns0:hi>Herodians</ns0:hi> (of whom we shall have occasion to say more when we come to <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 22.) all agree them, and the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> to have been steady Enemies one to another, but <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> can agree when Christ is to be <ns0:hi>Crucified.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 But when Jesus knew <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Chap. 10.23.</ns0:note> he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed him, and he healed them all.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.30.</ns0:note> charged them, that they should not make him known.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here is nothing in these two <ns0:hi>Verses,</ns0:hi> but what we have before met with: The multitudes have followed Christ in all his <ns0:hi>Motions,</ns0:hi> from his first beginning to preach, and to work his miraculous Operations. <ns0:hi>He healed them all,</ns0:hi> must be understood, of those that were <ns0:hi>Sick.</ns0:hi> The charge he gives is the same, which we have often met with, of which no satisfactory Account can be given, further than that knowing his time was not yet come, and he had much work to do before his Death, he useth all prudent means to preserve his Life, reserving himself for the further work which his Father left him to do. The publishing of his <ns0:hi>Miracles,</ns0:hi> would have made a great noise, and po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ibly have more inraged the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> against him, neither did he seek his own Glory, but the Glory of him that sent him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:239" />17 That it might be fulfilled, which was spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ke<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> by Isaias the prophet, saying.<ns0:note place="bottom">Christ did this, that is, he withdrew himself when he heard what Councels the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Herodians</ns0:hi> had taken, he Charged those w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>om he had cured, that they should not publish it abroad, he did those good Acts before spoken of, <ns0:hi>That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet.</ns0:hi> That he might shew himself to be the very Person, whom the Prophet <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> long since did foretel, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 42.1, 2, 3, 4. The words in the Prophet are thus. <ns0:hi>Behold my Servant whom I uphold, mine Elect in whom my Soul delighteth, I have put my Spirit upon him, he shall bring forth Iudgment to the Gentiles. He shall not Cry, nor lift up, nor cause his Voice to be heard in the Streets. A bruised Reed shall <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e not break, and the smoking Flax be shall not quench: He shall bring forth Iudgment unto Truth. He shall not fail, nor be discouraged, till he hath set Iudgment in the Earth, and the Isles shall wait for his Law.</ns0:hi> Thus far that Prophet, let us now consider his Words, or Prophecy, as repeated by the Evangelist.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 42.1.</ns0:note> Behold, my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.17. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.5.</ns0:note> in whom my Soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him; and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Alteration is very little, and we must not expect to meet with <ns0:hi>Quotations</ns0:hi> out of the Old Testament <ns0:hi>Verbatim</ns0:hi>: It is enough that the Sense is the same. <ns0:hi>Behold my Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant whom I have chosen<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> The word indifferently signifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth a <ns0:hi>Child</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Servant,</ns0:hi> Christ is called the Lords <ns0:hi>Servant,</ns0:hi> because he took upon him the <ns0:hi>Form of a Servant,</ns0:hi> and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />came <ns0:hi>Obedient</ns0:hi> even to Death, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.7, 8. <ns0:hi>Whom I have chosen, my Beloved in whom my Soul is well pleased,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>whom I uphold, mine Elect in whom my Soul delight<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth. Matthew</ns0:hi> seems to have left out <ns0:hi>whom I uphold,</ns0:hi> and to have taken the next Words, <ns0:hi>mine Elect</ns0:hi>: And to have tr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />slated them, <ns0:hi>whom I have chosen,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>as all said by the Prophet. God <ns0:hi>chose</ns0:hi> the Lord Jesus Christ to be our Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deemer, and the Head of the <ns0:hi>Elect,</ns0:hi> hence we are said to <ns0:hi>be chosen in him, Eph.</ns0:hi> 1.4. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> saith, he was <ns0:hi>Fore-ordained,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.20. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 2.6. he is<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> called <ns0:hi>a chief Corner st<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e, Elect, my Beloved in whom I am well pleased.</ns0:hi> In <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>in whom my Soul delighteth.</ns0:hi> The Sense is the same: <ns0:hi>He shall bring forth Iudgment to the Gentiles, or to the Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions.</ns0:hi> The Words <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>English</ns0:hi> are also variously used, as gives <ns0:hi>Interpreters</ns0:hi> a great Latitude to abound in their Senses. The most probable to me is this. <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies a thing adjudged: All Judgment is, either of <ns0:hi>Appro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bation,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Condemnation.</ns0:hi> He shall bring forth, or he shall shew the things, which God approveth and Judgeth right, both in matters of <ns0:hi>Doctrine, Worship,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Government of the Church of God,</ns0:hi> and in matters which concern the Government of mens Lives and Conversations<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and to this end God promiseth to put his <ns0:hi>Spirit upon him,</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.2. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 61.1. and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us, it was not given him by measure, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.34. which is the same, with being <ns0:hi>anointed with the Oyl of Gladness above his Fellows, Psal.</ns0:hi> 45.7. which the A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pos<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>le applieth to Christ, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 1.9.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 He shall not strive, nor cry, neither shall any man hear his voyce in the streets.<ns0:note place="bottom">These words declare the Meekness, and Gentleness, and modesty of our Blessed Saviour: His <ns0:hi>Meekness,</ns0:hi> that he should not do his work in any Passion, or Roughness, nor carry on his Kingdom with any Strife or Violence: Therefore when the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> took Councel against him, he made no oppo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sition, but Peaceably withdrew, until the time came when he was to be delivered, and then, he as meekly yielded up himself, rebuking <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> for but drawing a Sword for him, and heal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing his Ear which he had wounded. His not Crying, nor lifting up his Voyce, or suffering his Voyce to be heard in the Streets, might either signifie his <ns0:hi>Meekness,</ns0:hi> not Crying out to stir up any Sedition. Or not setting a <ns0:hi>Trumpet to his Mouth,</ns0:hi> when he had wrought a Miracle, that People might take notice of it, instead of it he Charged the Persons healed, not to publish it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 A bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, until he hath brought forth judgment unto victory.<ns0:note place="bottom">He shall carry on his work with so little noise, that if he trode upon a <ns0:hi>bruised Reed,</ns0:hi> he should not break it. Or he shall not despise the afflicted, that are as <ns0:hi>bruised Reeds,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>smoking</ns0:hi> Flax. But the best Expositors interpret it of Christ's <ns0:hi>kindness</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Peoples Souls.</ns0:hi> He will not discourage those that are weak in <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> or weak <ns0:hi>in Hope.</ns0:hi> Smoking Flax, sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ni<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eth Flax in the kindling of which the Fire hath not pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vailed, and so is a very apt Metaphor to express such as <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve,</ns0:hi> but are full of <ns0:hi>Doubts</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fears,</ns0:hi> or such as have a Truth of <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> but yet much Corruption; Christ is Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecied of, as one that will incourage, not discourage such Souls. <ns0:hi>Vntil he hath brought forth Iudgment into Victory, (Isaiah</ns0:hi> saith) <ns0:hi>unto Truth.</ns0:hi> Some think that, <ns0:hi>Vntil,</ns0:hi> here only signifies the Event of the thing, not a term of time, for there shall never be a time, when Christ shall break a <ns0:hi>bruised Reed,</ns0:hi> or quench a <ns0:hi>smoking Flax,</ns0:hi> in the Sense be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore mentioned. By <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> here may be meant, as be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, what his Father hath judged right, until he hath cau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed the Doctrine of the Gospel, and the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> to be be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved, and imbraced of all the World. Or, until he shall have brought forth the Judgment of those broken Reeds, and that smoking Flax into Victory, until such Souls be made perfect in Faith and Holiness, and shall have got a Victory over all its unbelief and other Corruptions. Or, until he hath brought forth <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ond<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>mnation into Victory (for so the word signifieth) till he hath Conquered <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hell,</ns0:hi> so as there shall be no Condemnation to any Soul that is in Christ Jesus, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.1. Or, <ns0:hi>Vntil the last Iudgment comes,</ns0:hi> which shall determine in a perfect absolution, and acquital of all his People, and in a perfect Victory over all his Enemies.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And in his name shall the Gentiles trust.<ns0:note place="bottom">This makes some think, that the bringing of Judgment into <ns0:hi>Victory,</ns0:hi> referreth to the final Destruction of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> after which the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> came more uni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versally to receive the Gospel. Tho Christ be <ns0:hi>Meek</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentle</ns0:hi> with men a long time, while there is any Hope of their Reformation: Yet, he will not be so meek and patient always. Neither was he so with the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> But the falling of them proved the rising of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; Christ is beholden to no People for bearing the Name of his Church; if the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> fail in their Duty, they shall be cast off, and <ns0:hi>in his Name shall the Gentiles trust.</ns0:hi> God is able of stones to raise up Children unto <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaiah</ns0:hi> saith, the <ns0:hi>Isles shall wait for his Law,</ns0:hi> his Law both of Faith and Hol<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ss, shall be acceptable to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> The term Law, here seem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to expound that Phrase, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18. <ns0:hi>He shall shew Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment to the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> that is right things, he shall give them his Law.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">See Chap 9.</ns0:note> Then was brought unto him one pos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sessed with a devil, blind and dumb, and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb, both spake and saw.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some think, this Person was the same mentioned, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.14. I presume, because the following Discourse there is much the same, with what followeth here, but others are of another mind; and it is certain <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> speaketh of no <ns0:hi>Blind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness in</ns0:hi> him. We heard before, a Discourse of such as were possessed by Devils, so as this Verse affords nothing new.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David?<ns0:note place="bottom">This is the first Conviction we met with, from the Miracles wrought by our Saviour. That he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> unless that of the two <ns0:hi>blind Men,</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.27. And their Faith in it appears but weak, for they do not plainly affirm it, only ask the Question like the Faith of those mentioned, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 7.31. <ns0:hi>When Christ cometh will he do more Miracles than this Man hath done?</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 But when the Pharisees heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they said, This <ns0:hi>f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>llow</ns0:hi> doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils.<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with the same Blasphemous Calumny, from the same Persons, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.34. The <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> not acknowledging the Deity of Christ, nor that he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> were for their Interest concerned, not to acknowledge, and as much as in them lay to keep others from believing, that he did that from his own Power, which God alone could do. But yet they might have allowed him to have by a Power derived from God, done these miraculous things, as <ns0:hi>Elijah and Elisha</ns0:hi> of old did. But they Blaspheme at the highest Rate imagina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, ascribing that to the Devil, which was proper to God alone. Christ's Miracles were exceeding many, and it was a time when the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was expected. The Scepter was de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />parted from <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and as it appears from <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 7.31, (what ever the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> now say impudently) They heard that when the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> did come, he should work many Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles. These things puts them into a Rage. This remarka<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble Piece of History is recorded by three Evangelists. By <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> in this place, by <ns0:hi>Mark ch.</ns0:hi> 3.22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30. and by <ns0:hi>Luke<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Ch.</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17, 18, 19, 20.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against it self is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against it self shall not stand.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And if Satan cast out Sa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>an, he is divided against himself, how shall then his kingdom stand?<ns0:note place="bottom">This is our Lords first Argument, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relates it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.23, 24, 25, 26. with little Alteration in the Phra<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> so doth <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.17, 18. The Sum of the Argument is, The Devil is so wise, that he will look to the upholding of his own Kingdom in the World. This will req<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ire an Agreement of the Devils among<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t themselves, for if they be divided they cannot uphold their Kingdom<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> nor stand any more than an house City, or Kingdom in the World so divided c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n stand, therefore the Prince of Devils will not forcibly cast out the infer<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>our De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vils. There is but one imaginable objection to this. Do we not see the contrary to this in Peoples going to Cunning<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men, for help against those that are bewitched, to get help for them, and is there no Truth in those many Stories we have of Persons that have found help against the Devil, from some that have Traded with the Devil? I Answer, It is one thing for the Devils to play one with another, another thing for them to Cast out one another. One Devil may yield, and give place to another, for to gain a greater advantage for the whole Society, but one never quarrelleth with another. The first may be for the inlarging or Satans Kingdom. This must be to destroy it. When a poor Wretched Creature go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to one, who dealeth with the Devil, for help for one who is vexed with some effect of the Devil, one Devil here doth but yield, and give place to another by Compact, Volunta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rily, and for the Devils greater advantage; for it is more advan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tage to the Devil (who seeks nothing so much as a Divine Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mage) to gain the Faith of one Soul, then to Exercise a Pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er to Afflict many Bodies. In such Cases as these, the Devil for the Abatement of a little bodily pain, gains a Power o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver the Soul of him or her, who cometh to implore his help, and exerciseth a Faith in him. This is an Establishing, pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moving and inlarging his Kingdom. But Christ forced the Devils out of Persons, they did not yield Voluntarily for a greater advantage, but forcibly, for no advantage. He did not pray the Devils to come out, nor make use of any of the <ns0:hi>Devils Sacraments,</ns0:hi> upon the use of which by some <ns0:hi>O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riginal Compact,</ns0:hi> he was obliged to come out, upon a Souls surrender of it self by Faith to him, but they came out un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />willingly upon the Authoritative Words of Christ, without the use of any <ns0:hi>Magical Rites,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ceremonies,</ns0:hi> testifying the least Homage done to him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:239" />27 And if I by <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">G<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:hi>Beelze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Beelzebub I cast out devils, by whom do your children cast <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> out? Therefore they shall be your Judges.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour's Argument is this, <ns0:hi>where the Case is the same, the Iudgment ought to be the same,</ns0:hi> and the contrary Judgment speaketh Malice, and Hatred of the Person. Do I <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ast out Devils? So do your Children. You say they do it by the Power of God, why do you say, that I do it by a Prince of Devils? What appeareth in their casting of them out more than in mine, which can argue that they do it by the Power of God, and I by the Power of the Prince of Devils? The on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly question is who our Saviour here meaneth by <ns0:hi>their Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren,</ns0:hi> some think that he meaneth his own Apostles, who were all of them Jews, and to whom they might be more favoura<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble then to him, because of their Relation to them. Others think that he means some <ns0:hi>Exorcists</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> such they had, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19.13. But concerning these there is a dou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble Opinion. Some think that they were such as themselves, Acted by Compact of the Devil. Others think that they In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vocating the God of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> God might Honour them so far, as upon that Invocation to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand the Devil out of Persons. <ns0:hi>Origen,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iustin Martyr</ns0:hi> both tell us, that there were some, that used that sorm, with such success. But so they might do, and yet not obtain their effect, from a <ns0:hi>Divine Influence,</ns0:hi> nor so much <ns0:hi>cast</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Flatter out</ns0:hi> Devils, upon an Homage first paid to the Devil. I find some Difficulty to persuade my self, that in those times, especially when God by this Miraculous effect, was Demonstrating the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> God should so far concur with any but him, and those that did it by his Express Name, and Authority, and I observe, that when the seven Sons of <ns0:hi>Sceva,</ns0:hi> attempted such a thing, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19.13. <ns0:hi>They called over them, which had E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil Spirits, in the name of the Lord Iesus, and said, we ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jure you by Iesus, whom</ns0:hi> Paul <ns0:hi>Preacheth</ns0:hi> (which they being the Sons of the Chief of the Priests<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> would not have done if the more grateful form of, The God of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> would have done it) yet could they not prevail (as you read there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14, 15, 16. (Our Saviours meaning there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore must certainly be either, 1. You do not say so of your Children, my Apo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>les, who do, and profess to do, what they do by a Power derived from me; why do you say this of me, not of them? 2. Or, There are some of you, who seem to cast out Devils, whenas the Devil only plays with them, and yields to their Magical Arts for his own Advantage, and a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bates some more External Effects, on Peoples Bodies, upon the Surrender of their Souls to him, by believing he is able to Cure them<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and imploring his help, yet you think these Men endowed with the Power of God: why are you so inequal to me? I observe, tho we read of <ns0:hi>Exorcists</ns0:hi> among<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t the Jews, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19.13. yet they are called <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Vagrants.</ns0:hi> They were an idle <ns0:hi>Vagabond</ns0:hi> sort of Persons (such probably as we call Gipsies) with whom, or by whom it is not proba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, God would Work such effects, especially at such a ti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e, tho they used the Names of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>Iac<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>b</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> N<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y it is plain from the Story of the <ns0:hi>Acts,</ns0:hi> that tho they used t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e Name <ns0:hi>Iesus,</ns0:hi> God would not Work by them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. The <ns0:hi>D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ack leapt upon them, overcame them, prevailed a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst them, so that they <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>led out of the House Naked, and Wounded.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath the same <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.20. only for <ns0:hi>the Spirit of God,</ns0:hi> he hath <ns0:hi>the Power of God.</ns0:hi> By the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> he here meaneth the <ns0:hi>coming of the Messiah,</ns0:hi> which is so called<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 2, 44. The time is come, when the Lord be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gins his <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Grace.</ns0:hi> Setting up <ns0:hi>his King upon his Holy Hill of Zion, Psal.</ns0:hi> 2.6. whence we may observe, that Christ giveth in his <ns0:hi>casting out of Devils,</ns0:hi> by a <ns0:hi>Divine Power, as an Argument to prove himself the Messiah</ns0:hi>; for saith he, By this you may know, the Kingdom of God is come among<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t you, that there is one come among you, who by the <ns0:hi>Finger,</ns0:hi> Power, or Spirit of God, calls out Devils. But where had the force of this Argument been, if the Jews had had <ns0:hi>Exorcists,</ns0:hi> whom God had so Honoured, tho <ns0:hi>Vagabonds,</ns0:hi> as to cast out Devils upon their calling upon the God of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> while in the mean time they derided, and contemned Christ?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Or else, how can one enter into a strong mans house, and spoyl his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoyl his house.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same words, with little Variation, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 3.27<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.21.22. saith, <ns0:hi>When a strong Man Armed<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> keepeth his Palace, his Goods are in peace. But when a stronger than he cometh upon him, and overcometh him, he taketh from him all his Armour, wherein he trusted, and divideth his Spoyl.</ns0:hi> The Sense is the same, tho the words be multiplyed. Our Saviour sheweth how his casting out of Devils, by the Spirit, and Power of God, argued that the <ns0:hi>Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siah</ns0:hi> was come, and the time come, when God would set up his Kingdom amongst Men. <ns0:hi>The Devil</ns0:hi> (saith he) who is the God of the World, and the Prince of the Power of the Air, is very strong, there is none save God only, who is stronger than he. If I were not God, I could ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver cast out this Strong Man, who Reigns in the World as in his House. As you see amongst Men, the Strong Man is not overcome, but by one stronger, he by this also lets them know, that he was so far from any <ns0:hi>Covenant</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Compact</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Beel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zebub,</ns0:hi> that he came into the World a Professed Enemy to him, to dispossess him of that Tyrannical Power he Exercised a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mong<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t Men, by his keeping them in Darkness, blinding them with Error, and Super<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tition, and seducing them to Sinful Practices, till God for their Prodigious Sins, had also given him a power over their Bodies, variously to Vex, Afflict, and Torment them. Christ took from this strong Man all his <ns0:hi>Armour</ns0:hi>: By <ns0:hi>scattering</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Darkness</ns0:hi> which was in the World, by the full Revelation of Gospel Truth: By <ns0:hi>Expel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling Error and Superstition,</ns0:hi> teaching People the Truths of God, and the right way of his Worship: By taking away the Guilt, and destroying the Power of Sin, and Death, <ns0:hi>Ig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />norance, Error, Profaneness.</ns0:hi> The Sense of the Guilt of Sin, and the Power of Lusts within us, being the Devils Armour, by which he kept up his Power, and doth yet keep up what Dominion he hath in the World.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 He that is not with me, is against me, and he that gathereth not with me, scattereth a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />broad.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath the same <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23. some understand this concerning the <ns0:hi>Devil,</ns0:hi> whom he was so far from favouring, that his Work was quite opposite. Some un<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>erstand it con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning some <ns0:hi>Neuters,</ns0:hi> that would neither shew themselves for Christ, nor against him. Our Saviour tells them, that this cause would bear no Neutrality, they must be either for him or against him. But po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sibly it is best understood, con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> whom he lets know; That he was one, shewed Men the true way of Life and Salvation, and those that complyed not with him, were his Enemies. And in stead of <ns0:hi>gathering, scattered</ns0:hi> the Sheep of God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin, and blasphemy, shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy <ns0:hi>against</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>holy</ns0:hi> Ghost, shall not be forgiven unto men.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 5.15.</ns0:note> but who<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever speaketh against the holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the <ns0:hi>world</ns0:hi> to come.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> repeateth the same <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29. with no Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teration as to the sense, and in stead of <ns0:hi>neither in this W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>rld, nor the World to come,</ns0:hi> he saith. <ns0:hi>But is in danger of eternal Damnation: Luke</ns0:hi> hath something of it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.10. <ns0:hi>And whosever shall speak a Word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him: But unto him that Blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven</ns0:hi>: It is a Text h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th very much exercised great Divines, and much more per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>exed poor C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tians in their <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>its of <ns0:hi>Melancho<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y,</ns0:hi> and un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der Temptations. T<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>er<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is in it something asserted, that is, <ns0:hi>That all manner of Sin,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>asphemy shall be forgiven,</ns0:hi> v. 32. <ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>os<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> ever shall speak a Word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven</ns0:hi> (that is, upon the terms other sins are forgiven, <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pentance</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Iesus Christ</ns0:hi>) By the <ns0:hi>Son of Man,</ns0:hi> here some would understand any ordinary Man, but, 1. Christ never spake of any under the Notion but himself. 2. It had been no great News for Christ to have told them, that ordinary <ns0:hi>Evil-speaking</ns0:hi> against men should be forgiven: Doubtless by the <ns0:hi>Son of Man</ns0:hi> here, Christ meaneth himself. He de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clareth that sins of Ignorance should be forgiven, tho a man should Blaspheme Christ, yet if he did it ignorantly, ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rily thinking he was no more than the <ns0:hi>Son of Man,</ns0:hi> it should upon his <ns0:hi>Repentance</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in him be forg<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ven. A Text yielding exceeding great relief to Souls, labouring under the Burden of their sins; and reflecting upon their Aggravation. But the Difficulty lyeth in the latter part of the Text, which denieth forgiveness to any, who <ns0:hi>Blaspheme the Holy Ghost</ns0:hi>: Upon this arise several Questions. 1. Quest. <ns0:hi>What the sin against the Holy Ghost here specified was. Ans.</ns0:hi> It is not hard to gather this from the Context, and what <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 30. <ns0:hi>Because they said he had an un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clean Spirit.</ns0:hi> Christ was come amongst these Persons to whom he speaketh, he had not only Preached, but he had wrought many miraculous Operations sufficient to convince them, that he Acted <ns0:hi>by the Power and Spirit of God.</ns0:hi> They were not only not convinced of it, so far as to acknowledge it, but they attributed these Operations to the Devil, and said he <ns0:hi>had a Devil,</ns0:hi> and that he did what he did, by the Power of the Devil. This out of doubt was their sin against the Holy Ghost, maliciously speaking to the highest Reproach of the Holy Spirit, contrary to the rational Conviction of thir own Consciences. Hence ariseth a second Question: <ns0:hi>Whether any such sin can be now committed. Ans.</ns0:hi> If there were no other but Texts that seem to conclude, there may such as those, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.4, 5, 6. <ns0:hi>& Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.26, 27. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 5.16. where he speak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth of a <ns0:hi>sin unto Death,</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Forgiveness</ns0:hi> of which he <ns0:hi>would not have Christians pray.</ns0:hi> I should conclude, that there is no <ns0:hi>such sin</ns0:hi> now to be committed, for we cannot have such <ns0:hi>means of Conviction</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had, Christ not being on the Earth now working Miracles. But it is plain from the Texts before mentioned, that there is such a sin, that Men and Women may yet incurr the Guilt of: But now what that <ns0:hi>sin is,</ns0:hi> hath exercised the Judgment of the greatest Divines to describe. I shall not repeat the various Opinions about it, many of which are easily confuted; but shall de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />termine from the Guidance of the Scriptures, that mention it so far as they will direct in the finding of it out. 1. It cannot be any sin that is committed ignorantly. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Blas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phemer,</ns0:hi> but forgiven, <ns0:hi>because he did it Ignorantly.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>It must be a sin knowingly committed, against the Operations of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> So was this sin of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>Apostacy</ns0:hi> must be an ingredient in it. <ns0:hi>If they fall away,</ns0:hi> saith the <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postle, Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.6. <ns0:hi>It is a sinning wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>fully after the receiving the knowledge of the Truth, Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.26. It should seem by this Text <ns0:hi>Persecution</ns0:hi> is an ingredient in it: The <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> did not only say this, but they spake it out of Malice, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signing to destroy Christ. 5. Most certain it is, that tho <ns0:hi>Impenitency</ns0:hi> cannot be called that sin, yet it must be an in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gredient in it, for what sins we truly repent of shall be forgi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.9. and therefore the Apostle saith of such sinners: It is <ns0:hi>impossible they should be renewed by Repentance.</ns0:hi> Upon the whole then, If any Person hath been instructed in the things of God, and hath made a Profession of Religion, and Godliness, and afterwards falleth off from his Profession, and becomes a bitter Enemy to it; saying that those things are the Effects of the Devil in Men, which his Heart telleth him are the Operations of the Holy Spirit, and be so hardy as to persecute and seek to destroy such Persons for such Professi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on: The Interpretation be to those that hate us, and to the Enemies of our God. If they have not committed this un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pardonable sin, they have done what is very like it, and I know no way they have, but by a timely and hearty Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pentance to satisfie the World, or their own Consciences, that they are not under this dreadful Guilt. And that which con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firms me in this Opinion, that we rarely hear of such Persons renewed by Repentance, (if any instances of that Nature at all can be produced.) I do know that some have thought that this <ns0:hi>Sin</ns0:hi> might be committed <ns0:hi>by Words,</ns0:hi> without other <ns0:hi>Ove<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>t-Acts,</ns0:hi> and indeed <ns0:hi>Blaspheming,</ns0:hi> (properly taken) can signifie nothing else, but <ns0:hi>Evil,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Reproachful speaking.</ns0:hi> But these words must proceed from a malitious Heart, full of Ran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or and Revenge, for it is not every word, nor every Blas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phemy, that is here meant, it is (as <ns0:hi>Augustine</ns0:hi> saith.) <ns0:hi>Quoddam dictum, quaedum b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>asphemia.</ns0:hi> A certain word, a certain Blasphe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />my: Not words spoken ignorantly, or <ns0:hi>hastily,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>according to our real Iudgment and Opinion</ns0:hi>: But words spoken <ns0:hi>malitiously</ns0:hi> in order to destroy God, or C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rist if it were po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sible; after sufficient means of Light and Co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>viction, that the things which we speak Evil of, are not from the Evil, (but pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably at least) from the Holy Spirit of God, and yet we will impute them to the Devil, in order to the defaming, or Destruction of those Servants of God, who do them, or in whom they are found. We can define nothing certain in the Case, but this cometh nearest to the sin here mentioned; that shall <ns0:hi>never be forgiven in this World, or the World to come</ns0:hi>: That is, as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> expounds it, the Persons Guilty, shall be <ns0:hi>in Danger</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>eternal Damnation,</ns0:hi> by which he hath spoiled the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> Argument from this Text for their <ns0:hi>Purgatory.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:240" />33 Either make the tree good, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 6.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 44.</ns0:note> his fruit good, or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt, for the tree is known by his fruit.<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.16. As the Words here spoken, may be understood to have reference to the <ns0:hi>De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vil,</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> or to <ns0:hi>Christ himself</ns0:hi>: You say, I do these things by the Devil, you cannot but say, the things I do are good, the Fruit followeth the Nature of the Tree: The Devil is Evil, a corrupt Tree, how can he pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duce good Fruit? Or thus, you shew your selves to be cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt Trees, by the Fruit you bring forth; you indeed are not Leud and Profane, but put on a Mask and Vizard of Godliness, but your Fruit sheweth what you are. Or, 3. If the Fruit which I produce be good, why should not you judge me good? Speak things that are consistent, if the Fruit be good, the Tree must be good, convince me of any Evil things that I do, from whence you can rationally conclude, that I am <ns0:hi>a Corrupt Tree.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 O Generation of Vipers! how can ye, being evil speak good things? For out of the abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dance of the heart, the mouth speaketh.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 A good man, out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: And an evil man out of the evil<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> treasure, bringeth forth evil things.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Evangelist <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.45. hath much the same with what is here, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35. <ns0:hi>O Generation of Vipers, Iohn</ns0:hi> had so called them, and Christ again so calleth them, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 23.23. A <ns0:hi>Viper</ns0:hi> is of all other the most <ns0:hi>Venemous,</ns0:hi> and dangerous Serpent. Christ in calling them, <ns0:hi>a Generation of Vipers,</ns0:hi> intimateth, that the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> were generally a most mischievous Faction, for the Souls of Men. <ns0:hi>How can ye, being Evil speak good things?</ns0:hi> Why do I (saith he) spend my time, and Breath in reproving, or admonishing you; you have cankred Hearts, full of <ns0:hi>Pride, Malice,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Envy,</ns0:hi> and therefore cannot ordinarily speak good things, for <ns0:hi>out of the abundance of the Heart, the Mouth speaketh.</ns0:hi> What Men ordinarily, and deliberately do speak, is from the Affecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, and Thoughts of their Hearts. Hence good Men out of the good Treasure of their Hearts, speak good things, that is, most ordinarily, and commonly, and Evil men, out of the stock of <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> Revenge, <ns0:hi>Envy, Pride,</ns0:hi> and other Lusts, which are in their Hearts, speak Evil things.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of in the day of judgment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some understand by <ns0:hi>Idle words</ns0:hi> here: Lying and <ns0:hi>deceit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Words,</ns0:hi> others <ns0:hi>Contumelious,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Reproachful words.</ns0:hi> But the best Interpreters here extend the Sense further, not only from the Sense of the word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, here used, but be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they judge our Saviour is here arguing, from the less to the greater, convincing the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> what a dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Acccount they had to give, for their Blasphemous, and Reproachful words, when all must give an Account even for those Words, which they speak to no good purpose, but vainly, without respect, either to the Glory of God, or the good of others, or their own necessary and lawful occasions. Hence the Apostle doth not only forbid <ns0:hi>Filthiness, foolish Talking,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iesting, Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.4. and <ns0:hi>corrupt Communication, Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.29. but in the same Verse, commandeth that Christians Speech should <ns0:hi>be to the use of Edifying, that it may minister Grace to the Hearers</ns0:hi>; and to the <ns0:hi>Colossians, Ch.</ns0:hi> 4.6. <ns0:hi>Let your Speech be always with Grace, seasoned with Salt.</ns0:hi> Nor will this seem too strict, to those who consider, that any thing is abused, when it is not used to the right end, and use. God hath not given unto Man his faculty of Speech, to fill the World with idle Tattle and impertinent Discourse, but that by it, 1. We might bless God, by Prayers, and Praises, Talking of his Words and wondrous Works. 2. That we might Communicate our minds to Men, in their or our own Concerns, and so be mutually helpful one to another. <ns0:hi>For by thy Words thou shalt be justified,</ns0:hi> &c. what <ns0:hi>justified</ns0:hi> here s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>gnifies, appears by the word <ns0:hi>Condemned</ns0:hi> (to which it is op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed,) God will pronounce Sentence, for or against Men in the last day, not only according to their other Actions, but according to their other Actions, but accordingly as they have used their Tongues. If there were no other Text in the Bi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, to prove that we have need of another Righteousness, than any of our own, wherein to stand before God, this Text alone would be enough, for <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 3.2. <ns0:hi>If a Man of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fend not in Word, the same is a perfect man.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:240" />38 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 8.11. Luke 11.16. 1 Cor. 1.22.</ns0:note> Then certain of the scribes, and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee.<ns0:note place="bottom">We read the like to this, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 16.1. and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> seemeth to relate the same History, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 11.29. <ns0:hi>Master</ns0:hi> was the usual Title, which they gave to any whom they owned as a Teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er. By a <ns0:hi>Sign,</ns0:hi> they mean some thing that might confirm unto them, that he was sent of God; they expected, that an Extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinary Mission should be so confirmed, so <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.30. <ns0:hi>What Sign shewest thou then, that we might see, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve thee, what doest thou Work? Moses</ns0:hi> shewed them signs (as they there go on) he brought down for them <ns0:hi>Bread from Heaven.</ns0:hi> Had not Christ shewed them Signs enough, what were all the Miracles he had wrought in their sight? They ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther speak this out of a further Idle Curiosity (their Eye being not satisfyed with seeing) or else they speak it in direct op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />position, to the whole Scope and Tendency of our Saviour's <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer Discourse, which was from his Miracles to prove him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self truly God, and sent of God: if the latter which seemeth from our Saviours sharp Answer, most probable, the Sum of what they say, is this. <ns0:hi>Master</ns0:hi> we have seen thee do won<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derful Works, but no other than what Impostors may do by the assistance of the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi>; we would see something done by thee, which <ns0:hi>Magicians</ns0:hi> cannot do, such as <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 8.19. when the Magicians confessed they were out done, and cryed, <ns0:hi>This is the Finger of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
