                  </ns0:gap> man be three days and three nights in the heart o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> the earth.<ns0:note place="bottom">An Evil, and <ns0:hi>Adulterous Generation.</ns0:hi> Either called Adul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />terous, for that Specifical Sin, which reigned amongst them and indeed their <ns0:hi>Polygamy</ns0:hi> was hardly better: or else because of their Degeneracy from <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> whom they so much glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />ryed in as their Father, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>39.44. <ns0:hi>Seeketh after a Sign,</ns0:hi> not satisfyed with my Miracles which I do on <ns0:hi>Earth,</ns0:hi> they would have a <ns0:hi>Sign from Heaven.</ns0:hi> God was not diffi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cult of Confirming, and incouraging Peoples <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Signs.</ns0:hi> He gave <ns0:hi>Gideon</ns0:hi> a Sign upon his asking<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> he gave <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> and profered <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> a Sign without asking. But he had al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />ready given the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Signs enough, and sufficient to Convince them, but they would not believe, but out of Cu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riosity would have a Sign of another kind, a Sign from Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> expoundeth it, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.11. such a Sign as the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> could not Counterfeit. <ns0:hi>There shall no Sign be give<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to it,</ns0:hi> no Sign of that Nature, for we shall find that after this Christ wrought many Miracles. But they shall have a Sign when I shall be risen again from the Dead, to their Confusion and Condemnation. When I shall Answer the Prophet <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nas</ns0:hi> his Type of me. He was cast into the Sea, and was three days and three nights in the Belly of the Whale, in the Heart of the Sea, <ns0:hi>Ionas</ns0:hi> 1.17. and then the <ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ale Vomited him out upon the dry Land, ch.</ns0:hi> 2. So I shall be by them violently put to Death, and shall be in the Grave part o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> three Days and three Nights, and then I shall rise again from the Dead. But here ariseth a difficulty. Christ indeed dying the Day before the <ns0:hi>Iewish Sabbath,</ns0:hi> and rising the Morning after, might be said to be in the Grave three Days, because he was there part of three Days, but how can he be said to have been there <ns0:hi>three Nights</ns0:hi>? for he was only in the Grave the Night of the Jewish Sabbath. (For their S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>bbath began at the Evening before) and the Night following, which were but two Nights, either in whole, or in part. Ans. what we call Day and Night, made up the Jewish <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. It appears by <ns0:hi>Genesis</ns0:hi> 1.5. That the <ns0:hi>Evening and Morning made up a Day.</ns0:hi> Three Days, and three Nights is with us but the same thing with three Natural Days, and so it must be under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tood here. Christ was in the Grave three <ns0:hi>Natural Days,</ns0:hi> that is, part of three Natural Days. Every one of which Days con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained a Day and a Night, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> 24. hours.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 The men of Nineveh shall rise in judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment with this generation, and condemn it, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they repented at the preaching of Jonas, and behold a greater then Jonas <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> here.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Story of the men of <ns0:hi>Nineveh</ns0:hi> we have in <ns0:hi>Ionah, Ch.</ns0:hi> 35. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> repeateth the same Passage, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 11.32. The Men of <ns0:hi>Nineveh shall rise in Iudgment,</ns0:hi> that is, shall at the General Resurrection, rise, and stand up in <ns0:hi>Iudgment</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nesses</ns0:hi> against the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> and the o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther unbelieving <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> of this Age, and shall be Instruments, as to that Condemnation, which God shall that Day pronounce against them. Why? <ns0:hi>Beca<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>se they repented at t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e P<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>each<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of</ns0:hi> Jonas, <ns0:hi>and behold a greater than</ns0:hi> Jonas <ns0:hi>is here. I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nas</ns0:hi> was a Stranger to them, he wrought no Miracles a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ongst them, to confirm that he was sent of God, he only came and cry<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, <ns0:hi>yet forty days,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nd <ns0:hi>Nineveh shall be destroyed,</ns0:hi> yet they Repented, if not <ns0:hi>truly</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>sincerely,</ns0:hi> yet in appearance, they shewed themselves to be affected with what <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nah</ns0:hi> said, his Words made some impressions upon them, as that the <ns0:hi>King a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rose from his Throne, laid his R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>be from him, covered him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self with Sackcloth, and sate in Ashes, called a Fast,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nah</ns0:hi> 3.5, 6, 7, 8. but saith our Saviour, I am greater than <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nah</ns0:hi>; I was long since Prophesied of, and foretold to this People, to Come; I am Come, I have Preached amongst them, and not only Preached, but wrought many wonderful Works amongst them, yet they are not so much affected, as to shew the least Signs of Repentance.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 11.31.</ns0:note> The Queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it, for she came from the uttermost parts ofthe earth, to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold a greater than Solomon <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> here.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have the History to which this relateth, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 10.1. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> she is here called the <ns0:hi>Queen of the South,</ns0:hi> in the Book of <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> and 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 9.1. the Queen of <ns0:hi>Sheba,</ns0:hi> whether this <ns0:hi>S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>eba</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Saba</ns0:hi> was in <ns0:hi>Arabia</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ethiopia,</ns0:hi> is not much M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>terial; certain it is, it was <ns0:hi>Southward</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> and a place at a great distance. Yet saith our Saviour, Tho She was a great <ns0:hi>Queen,</ns0:hi> tho she lived at so great a distance from <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem,</ns0:hi> tho She had only heard of the Fame and Wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom of <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi>: Yet She came in Person to hear his wise Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courses<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> either about things Natural or Super-natural. T<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ese Wretched Jews are not put to it to take a journy, I am come <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>mongst them, I who am greater than <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> who am the <ns0:hi>Eternal Wisdom,</ns0:hi> and come to Discourse of Heavenly Wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom to them; I am come to their Doors, the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r's, to whom the Notion of a <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> is no new thing, they have heard of me, they are no Heathens, but bred up to the knowledge of God. I have done many Miracles before them, yet they will not he<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r, nor believe me. The Queen of <ns0:hi>Sheba</ns0:hi> in the day of Judgment shall rise up as a Witness against them, when God shall Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demn them for their unbelief. The more Light, and Means, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nd Obligat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ons Men have upon them, to Faith and Holiness, the greater will their Judgment, and Condemnation be.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 11.24.</ns0:note> When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 1.7.</ns0:note> he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 Then he saith, I will return unto my house, from whence I came out, and when he is come, he findeth <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> empty, swept, and garnished.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then goeth he, and taketh with himself se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven other spirits more wicked then himself and they enter in, and dwell there, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 6.4. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.26.</ns0:note> and the last state of that man, is worse then the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Speech appeareth <ns0:hi>Parabolical</ns0:hi>; the Persons concerned in it are expressed in the last Words. <ns0:hi>The Men of that wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d Generation.</ns0:hi> The Text is thought to be well expound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed by <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.20. <ns0:hi>If after they have escaped the Pollution of the World, through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Iesus Christ, they are entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning.</ns0:hi> Our Lord here compare<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>h the Jews to a Man out of whom the unclean Spirit was gone. The Devil is called the unclean Spirit, both in regard of his own impure Nature and because his Work is to tempt Men to Sin, (which is Spiritual filthiness.) The Jews were a People holy to the Lord, a peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple distinguished from <ns0:hi>Pagans,</ns0:hi> by a visible <ns0:hi>Profession.</ns0:hi> So as the Devil in a great Measure had left them. Now saith he, the Devil is an unquiet Spirit, and findeth no rest, if he can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not be doing Mischief to Men. For the Phrase, <ns0:hi>He walk<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth through dry places, looking for rest,</ns0:hi> we must know, That in Parabolical Speeches, we must not Scrue, or make a severe Scrutiny upon every Phrase. <ns0:hi>Dry places</ns0:hi> are for the most part places least inhabited, for want of the Convenien<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cies of Water. The Devil cannot be at rest, where he hath no Mischief to do to Men. Then he saith, <ns0:hi>I will return to my House, from which I came out.</ns0:hi> The Devil so leaveth none, but he will be attempting to come into them again, and he ordinarily succeedeth where Christ hath not prepossest the Soul, all other Reformation proves but a <ns0:hi>Sweeping</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishing,</ns0:hi> while the Soul is empty of Christ. It may be swept from the filth of Flagitious Sins, and Garnished with the Paint of Religion, or some Habits of Moral Vertue. But none of these will keep out the Devil. <ns0:hi>He goeth and taketh with himself, seven Spirits more wicked than himself, and enters in and dwelleth there. Seven,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>many.</ns0:hi> The mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing is, he makes that Man much worse than before. So (saith he) it shall be to these <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> God gave them his Laws, and so delivered them from such a Dominion, as the Devil doth exercise over <ns0:hi>Pagans.</ns0:hi> In Force of this Law, the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> amended many things, so as they were like an House <ns0:hi>swept</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>garnished.</ns0:hi> God sent his Son to <ns0:hi>dwell</ns0:hi> amongst them, but him they rejected, so the House was <ns0:hi>empty,</ns0:hi> tho swept and garnished. The Devil will come again, and they will be ten times worse.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:241" />46 While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren, stood without, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siring to speak with him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Then one said unto him, Behold, thy mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther and thy brethren stand without, desiring to speak with thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 But he answered, and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And he stretched forth his hand towards his disciples and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Joh. 15.14. Gal. 5.6. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 6.15. Col. 3.11.</ns0:note> whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and sister, and mother.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> repeateth the same passage, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 3.31, 32, 33, 34, 35. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> repeateth it more shortly, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 8.20.21. Both <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, more than one spake to our Saviour, first one, then others. <ns0:hi>Thy Mother and t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y Brethren,</ns0:hi> most Interpreters think <ns0:hi>Brethren</ns0:hi> here signifieth, no more than some of his <ns0:hi>Kindred,</ns0:hi> whom the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> usually called <ns0:hi>Brethren.</ns0:hi> By the following words of our Saviour, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 48, 49, 50. we must not under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tand that our Saviour slighted his <ns0:hi>Mother</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Brethren,</ns0:hi> we are elsewhere taught what Honour he gave to his Parents, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.51. yet he seemeth to speak something angerly, because he was interrupted in his work, so <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.49. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2, 3, 4. we may shew a just Respect to our <ns0:hi>Parents,</ns0:hi> and Respect to our Relations, tho we do not neglect our Duty to God, out of Respect to them. The only thing to be further learned from this <ns0:hi>Paragraph,</ns0:hi> is how dear <ns0:hi>Believers,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Holy Persons are to Christ.</ns0:hi> He counts them as dear as <ns0:hi>Mother, Brethren,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sisters,</ns0:hi> and thereby teacheth us the Esteem, we ought to have for such, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He that heareth my Word, and doth it. Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, he that <ns0:hi>doth it</ns0:hi>: It is the Will of God, that we should believe on him whom he hath sent: See <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 6.40. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 1.12. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 8.47. This Text derogates nothing from the Honour truly due to the Blessed Virgin; as the Mother of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> but it shews the madness of the <ns0:hi>Papists,</ns0:hi> ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />alting her above Christ, whom Christ (considered only as his Mother) seemeth here to set beneath every true Believer, tho, considered as a Believer also, she hath a just preference.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
